correctness.rationale: Correct for every m>n>=2: separating singleton multipliers proves that marginal pairs have identical support; the precise within-support condition follows from marginality of AB* and B*A and Duan--Zhang’s independently checked explicit margin classification. Conjugating one primitive phase at a rank-n endpoint-supported diagonal generates every decorated support fiber, while singleton idempotent conjugates prove maximal idempotent separation. Exact class and pair counts follow from choices of domains and ranges. A standalone exhaustive checker tested seven (m,n) pairs, all within-support defining equations, rank-one separation, and closure of the proposed principal generating pair; finite checks are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: For the nonnormal regime m>n, the inspected source proves only that marginal equivalence is strictly smaller than its generated congruence. It neither identifies the entire generated kernel nor counts all equivalence classes or gives a principal generator. These follow by a new phase-transport argument combined with a complete within-support comparison. Related full partial-monomial and partial-wreath results operate on different semigroups and relations. Historical priority is not certified; some conclusions are short corollaries of known inputs.
residual_risks: The result is a short mathematical consequence of Duan--Zhang’s explicit margin criterion plus phase-transport; equivalent unlabelled or maximal-idempotent-separating descriptions may be familiar or published without using marginal terminology.
The comparison with broader historical inverse-semigroup literature is targeted rather than exhaustive.
No independent audit of the universal proof has been conducted.

value.rationale: The motivating work’s nonnormal counterexamples explicitly separate marginal equivalence from marginal congruence. Determining the complete generated congruence, its minimal one-pair generating mechanism, every marginal class, and the sharp fixed-exponent class-pair ratio answers the natural next structural question for the entire two-parameter counterexample family. The result is motivated by an established marginal-relations problem and determines canonical quotient data, not a computationally arbitrary slice.
